One comment was not relevant to the proposed specifications and is not discussed further.
v2_only_examples.response: The comment is not discussed further as it is not relevant to the proposed specifications.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: Kohler Company petitioned the EPA for reconsideration of the final rule for Clay Ceramics Manufacturing, which led to the proposal of revisions to the NESHAP on August 20, 2018.
rows.response: The EPA is finalizing the revisions to the NESHAP, incorporating changes in response to Kohler's petition and public comments, to provide flexibility to the clay ceramics manufacturing industry while maintaining emissions and operational standards.

rows.label: NORMATIVE-RICH
rows.comment: One commenter (EPA-HQ-OPPT-2023-0456-0005) expressed concern over the "reporting limit issue" created by the proposed dust-lead hazard standard (88 FR 50444) and encouraged EPA to amend the LQSR to allow laboratories to have reporting limits above their method detection limit (MDL) without requiring the MDL multiplier.
rows.response: EPA disagrees that 50% of zero would have been the reporting limit under the dust-lead proposal. However, in response to concerns, EPA modified LQSR 4.0's Section 5.3 Test and Sampling Methods to require NLLAP-recognized laboratories to achieve a quantitation limit "equal to or less than . . . 80% of the lowest action level (i.e., regulatory limit) for dust wipe samples".

rows.label: NORMATIVE-RICH
rows.comment: The commenter stated that EPA must take action on Missouri's submission regarding interstate transport. The commenter asserted that the Cross State Air Pollution Rule (CSAPR) update does not cover all sources of interstate transport and that in EPA's own words is only a ``partial remedy'' for transport related to the ozone NAAQS. The commenter thus argued that EPA must address the remainder of Missouri's contribution to ambient ozone levels in neighboring states in this rulemaking and that EPA has a nondiscretionary duty to issue a Federal Implementation Plan (FIP) when a state fails to submit an approvable state SIP submission.
rows.response: EPA stated it was not taking action on the good neighbor provisions in section 110(a)(2)(D)(i)(I) as Missouri did not address these requirements in its infrastructure SIP submission. EPA acknowledged the commenter's concerns and noted it has already taken steps to address interstate transport with the CSAPR update and will take further steps in a separate action.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: In a letter to the Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation of July 20, 1995, the Clean Air Coalition suggested that importing low-sulfur diesel fuel is a low cost option to comply with the low-sulfur highway diesel fuel requirement, since highway diesel fuel
rows.response: Not explicitly stated in the provided document, but the EPA discusses the challenges and costs of transporting and storing low-sulfur diesel fuel in Alaska, implying that importing it may not be a feasible or cost-effective solution.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: Four commenters provided substantive comments
rows.response: The Agency's responses to the principal comments are provided below. The remaining comments are addressed in the Response to Comments document available in the docket for this action.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: Eight commenters expressed support for the proposal. Several of the supporters wrote that restricted areas R-6604D and R-6604E abut, but do not include, VOR Federal airway V-139, concluding, when those areas are in use, air traffic can continue to flow unimpeded on the airway.
rows.response: The FAA notes that R-6604D and R-6604E infringe upon the 4-NM width on the east side of the airway centerline, making the airway unusable below 4,000 feet MSL when either area is active. Alternative routes are available.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: Fernando Campos of KACALP Flight Operations requested that the requirements of the new revisions to the Limitations section of the FAA-approved maintenance program (e.g., maintenance manual) be written into the AD instead of requiring operators to insert these new revisions into the Limitations section of the FAA-approved maintenance program (e.g., maintenance manual).
rows.response: The FAA does not agree with the commenter. Although some operators may or may not own a current hardcopy subscription of the Pilatus PC-12 maintenance library (e.g., maintenance manual), 14 CFR 21.50 requires that a complete set of instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) be delivered with the airplane. Therefore, it is possible for an operator to comply with paragraph (f)(1) of this AD using the set of ICA delivered with the airplane.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: Horizon Air asked that the requirement to do the actions specified in paragraph (k) of the proposed AD in accordance with paragraph 3.A. of the Accomplishment Instructions of Bombardier Service Bulletin 84-32-154, Revision A, dated November 21, 2018, be removed. Horizon Air stated that the job setup specified in paragraph 3.A. of the referenced service information does not directly correct the unsafe condition. Horizon Air would like only the actions specified in paragraph 3.B. of the referenced service information mandated.
rows.response: The FAA does not agree with the commenter's request. The job setup actions are necessary to adequately perform the corrective actions and prevent damage to equipment.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: Air Line Pilots Association, International (ALPA) stated that it supports the NPRM.
rows.response: The FAA acknowledged ALPA's support and determined that air safety and the public interest require adopting the final rule as proposed, except for minor editorial changes.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: The commenter requested the FAA consider how passengers will be made aware of what the commenter described as the ``unique'' configuration of a fuel tank directly under passenger seats in what is traditionally a location for baggage and cargo. The commenter suggested that the FAA make passengers aware of their proximity to the airplane fuel.
rows.response: The FAA informed the public of the proposed configuration in the Notice of Proposed Special Conditions No. 25-23-06-SC and stated that the configuration is not unique, as many transport airplanes have fuel tanks near passengers. No changes were made to the special conditions.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: Several third parties have objected to the use of the data center pole for the Wireless Connections. They argue that IDS has an advantage over its competitors because third parties are not allowed access to the data center pole, and the data center pole is closer to the Mahwah data center than any commercial pole.
rows.response: The Exchange proposes a new rule to place restrictions on the use of the data center pole, requiring that the length of the connection from the data center pole to the network row in the co-location space be no less than the length of the connection from the closest commercial pole to the same point, thereby addressing the competitive disparity.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: The Commission has received several requests for an extension of time for public comment on the proposal to, among other things, allow for adequate time to fully consider the proposals and to improve the quality of responses.
rows.response: The Commission is reopening the comment period for Release Nos. 33-10569; 34-84508; IC-33286 until March 15, 2019, to provide the public additional time to thoroughly consider the matters addressed by the release and to submit comprehensive responses.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: One commenter praised "the significant steps taken to improve the masking methodology" for the Pilot data.
rows.response: The Commission appreciates the comment and believes that FINRA's proposal is consistent with the requirements of the Act and would further the purpose of the Plan to provide measurable data.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: Several commenters suggest that the Proposed Rule Change's failure to include a requirement that FICC's direct participants offer done-away clearing services would not sufficiently provide for a workable done-away model.
rows.response: The Commission disagrees, stating that a done-away mandate could expose FICC and its participants to unique risks, such as liquidity risks, and could be counterproductive, ultimately discouraging Netting Member intermediaries from providing clearing services to customers.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: One commenter stated that the proposal's requirements with respect to maintaining end-of-day security ownership balances on the blockchain are inconsistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because the maintenance of these records does not appear to be necessary for the clearance and settlement of these securities, the fair and orderly trading of securities, or any purpose regulated by the Act.
rows.response: The Exchange responded that the proposal would allow market participants to observe and increase their familiarity with the capabilities and potential benefits of blockchain technology in a context that parallels current equity market infrastructure and thereby advance and protect the public's interest in the use and development of new data processing techniques that may create opportunities for more efficient, effective and safe securities markets.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: Dr. Fleming presented three reasons for terminating his debarment: (1) that he was effectively debarred in the period between when he was convicted of the two felony offenses on which his debarment was based and when FDA finalized his debarment; (2) that he has taken training courses related to billing and ethics; and (3) that he has taken steps to prevent future mistakes in billing and collecting data.
rows.response: The Chief Scientist agrees with ORA that Dr. Fleming's arguments do not justify terminating his debarment, as his felony fraud convictions indicate a threat to the drug approval process and his corrective measures are insufficient to demonstrate he can comply with the FD&C Act.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: One respondent stated that it was unclear whose burden had been measured for the estimate and stated that information about methodology and assumptions was insufficient for it to comment.
rows.response: The agency noted that its estimate was based on contacts with industry representatives and that the comment did not provide an alternative estimate, so the agency's estimate remains the same.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: One comment questioned the necessity of this proposed collection.
rows.response: FDA believes that this proposed collection is necessary in keeping with the Agency's mission of ensuring the safety and efficacy of human drugs.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: 1. In section 2.5.1. AB enzymes state that the enzyme preparation is light beige powder and in Attachment 1 the results from representative the batch analyses are from a liquid enzyme concentrate. Please clarify the discrepancy and describe the manufacturing steps to produce a powdered fructanase enzyme preparation. Please confirm that the results from the batch analyses of the liquid concentrate are representative of powder form in section 2.5.1.
rows.response: AB Enzymes explained that the liquid enzyme concentrate is the purest form of the enzyme before formulation with sunflower oil and wheat flour, and that the differences between the liquid and powder forms are enzyme activity levels and the presence of formulation ingredients. They confirmed that the results from the batch analyses of the liquid concentrate are representative of the powder form.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: In the Federal Register of September 13, 2018 (83 FR 46501) FDA published a 60-day notice requesting public comment on the proposed collection of information. Two PRA related comments were received, which inquired about how FDA formulated the PRA estimates.
rows.response: In response to the questions related to the PRA estimates, these estimates are based on our experience. To date, the annual number of exemption requests has been lower than the estimate of 812 respondents in this notice, but the Agency expects that the number of exemption requests could increase as applicants begin to submit such requests for tobacco products subject to the final deeming rule.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: One commenter agreed that the commercial sector allocation for Atlantic dolphin (dolphin) should be increased, but suggested that the methods used to calculate the allocation changes need to be revisited. Another commenter suggested that the Council should select a different alternative that allocates 86 percent of the total ACL to the recreational sector and 14 percent to the commercial sector.
rows.response: The Council used more recent commercial and recreational landings from 2008 through 2012, resulting in a revised allocation of 10% for the commercial sector and 90% for the recreational sector. The Council determined this change reduces the potential for exceeding the commercial ACL and meets the objectives of the Generic AM Amendment and the Dolphin Wahoo FMP.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: There were 74 unique comments submitted in favor of the action. Of these, 13 were from recreational fishing/diving organizations and 61 were from individuals. One of the comments from an organization included 4,301 signatures in support of the action. In addition, we received 263 form letters from individuals in support of the action.
rows.response: NMFS acknowledges the support and has implemented the SMZs as proposed, with some corrections to the coordinates for the Ocean City and Shark River Reef Sites.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: The commercial trip limit for gag should be reduced to 100 or 150 lb (45 or 68 kg) instead of 300 lb (136 kg), which would allow the commercial fishing season to stay open longer. This would reduce regulatory discards of gag when other snapper-grouper species such as greater amberjack are targeted.
rows.response: NMFS acknowledges the importance of gag to the seafood market and commercial fishermen's preference to maintain access to as many species as possible throughout the year. The majority of commercial trips from 2017 through 2019 that landed gag with at least 1 lb of gag landed less than the 300 lb trip limit being implemented through this final rule.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: We received six comments from private citizens, with five expressing general support for the project and one expressing general opposition to the project.
rows.response: NMFS acknowledges the comments, but does not provide a detailed response to the opposition comment as the document does not specify the reasons for opposition.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: If the commercial or recreational season is projected to be 3 days or less, it is better for the stock in the long term to not open the season.
rows.response: NMFS acknowledges that allowing harvest during a short season could result in higher fishing mortality, but notes that overall harvest is limited by ACLs and accountability measures, and thus, the stock is not expected to be negatively impacted.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: Hughes contends that low-latency, high-speed bids will always necessarily win. Bids will be scored relative to the reserve price and therefore bids placed for lower speeds and high latency will have the opportunity to compete for support, but will have to be particularly cost-effective to compete with higher tier bids.
rows.response: The Commission disagrees, stating that bids will be scored relative to the reserve price, allowing lower-speed, high-latency bids to compete if they are cost-effective. The Commission also notes that adopting minimal weights, as Hughes proposes, could deprive rural consumers of higher-speed, lower-latency services.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: The majority of commenters support eliminating Form 325.
rows.response: The Commission agrees and concludes that eliminating Form 325 will advance the Commission's goal of reducing outdated rules and unnecessary regulatory burdens.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: ATIS's petition for reconsideration of the Second Report and Order & Further Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (FNPRM), which requested clarification on the scope of the suspension of Network Outage Reporting System (NORS) reporting obligations during DIRS activations.
rows.response: The Commission granted ATIS's petition in part, clarifying that NORS reporting is waived for outages occurring after the first DIRS filing deadline, but denied the request to extend the waiver to 911 and 988 special facility notifications, citing procedural and substantive concerns.

rows.label: SUBSTANTIVE-DRY
rows.comment: Some commenters believed the notice period should commence upon application filing
rows.response: The Commission modified its proposal to commence the notice period no later than five business days after release of the Commission's public notice accepting filing of the application, as the time period for filing petitions to deny commences on the date of acceptance.

rows.label: PERFUNCTORY
rows.comment: Some commenters argued that reporting outage information imposes no additional costs on carriers.
rows.response: The Commission disagrees, stating that even if a carrier has information readily available, preparing and submitting duplicative documentation entails costs.
